papers.title: Active Learning for Approximation of Expensive Functions with Normal Distributed Output Uncertainty
papers.abstract: When approximating a black-box function, sampling with active learning focussing on regions with non-linear responses tends to improve accuracy. We present the FLOLA-Voronoi method introduced previously for deterministic responses, and theoretically derive the impact of output uncertainty. The algorithm automatically puts more emphasis on exploration to provide more information to the models.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的主动学习方法可直接用于提高代理模型在不确定条件下的采样效率，可迁移至植入物设计中的昂贵仿真近似。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical or implant-specific context, no FEA surrogate integration or biomechanical constraint handling.

summary_en.motivation: To improve sampling efficiency when approximating expensive black-box functions with noisy outputs.
summary_en.method: Extended the FLOLA-Voronoi active learning algorithm to handle normally distributed output uncertainty with a theoretical analysis of its impact.
summary_en.result: The algorithm automatically shifts emphasis toward exploration to provide more informative samples.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical derivation of the effect of output uncertainty on the acquisition function.
